headline: Cloudflare is buying Deno, the start-up co-founded by Node.js creator Ryan Dahl, and will end development of Deno's own runtime and hosting service.
score_reason: Confirmed acquisition of a known developer-tools company, but small and no price disclosed.
importance_line: Affects developers who use Deno, who have six months to move hosted apps, and gives Cloudflare an experienced team for running AI agents; the article gives no price, and the open-source promises so far rest on statements by Dahl and Cloudflare.
summary: The New Stack reports that Cloudflare announced on Friday that the whole team behind Deno, a JavaScript and TypeScript runtime (software that runs that code), is joining it; Deno's standalone runtime and Deno Deploy hosting service will be wound down, with the runtime getting maintenance and security updates for a year and Deno Deploy closing in six months. The team will merge Deno's open-source Celld project, which recreated Cloudflare's Workers serverless model, with Cloudflare's own open-source runtime Workerd, which Cloudflare engineer Kenton Varda said had not been made practical to run outside Cloudflare's network.
notes: Read in full via The New Stack.
